criteria.rationale: The notice text and receipt timestamp are stored together as fields of the same immutable Notice dataclass and within the same database table row. Both fields are always created together in the receive method, retrieved together via the get method, and the delete_expired method removes complete Notice objects atomically. This design maintains the required association throughout the retention period, ensuring the notice text is kept with its receipt timestamp.

decision.rationale: The system is designed as a notice service for operators with statutory retention requirements, as evidenced by the README stating it 'stores notices received by an operator and retains them for the configured statutory retention period.' This design indicates the system is intended for entities offering the notice service to the public, not for private household use. Therefore, the retention requirements apply.

criteria.rationale: The system has a critical non-compliance: the delete_expired method calculates expiration using draft_timestamp + RETENTION_PERIOD (line 43), but the legal requirement mandates retention be calculated from receipt_timestamp. While the retention period duration is correctly set to 7 days and temporary test records are properly exempted, using the wrong timestamp base means records may be deleted before the legally required 7 days from receipt have elapsed.

facts.statement: This is a notice service that stores notices received by an operator, retaining them for a configured statutory retention period. The service stores notice text, receipt timestamp, draft timestamp, and a flag indicating whether records are temporary test records. Temporary test records are excluded from normal retention processing. Deployment exposure (publicly reachable vs private/internal only) is an operator/environment decision not stored in this repository.
The system configures a retention period of 7 days (timedelta(days=7)) which meets the minimum 7-day requirement.

The delete_expired method calculates record expiration using draft_timestamp + RETENTION_PERIOD instead of receipt_timestamp + RETENTION_PERIOD, which does not comply with the legal requirement that retention must be calculated from the receipt timestamp.
Temporary test records (is_temporary_test=True) are excluded from the retention deletion logic, satisfying the exception for temporary test records.

Notice text and receipt timestamp are stored together as fields of the same Notice dataclass (frozen/immutable) and in the same database table row, maintaining their association throughout storage and retrieval. The deletion logic operates on complete Notice objects, ensuring associated data is removed together.

The Notice dataclass is defined as frozen (immutable), preventing any modification of notice_text after creation. The NoticeService provides no methods to update or modify stored notices; it only supports creation (receive), retrieval (get), and deletion (delete_expired). No text sanitization, filtering, truncation, or transformation logic exists in the codebase.
